text:
Taylor (Sales): Hey team, Opsidian wants the SIG Q-by-Q evidence bundle for their Private POC. Procurement asked for artifacts + short answers for Q10 (data location), Q29 (network isolation), Q44 (encryption at rest), and Q76 (third-party subprocessors). Can we get an export by Thu EOD PT?

Sam (Solutions Eng): I’ll handle Q10 and Q29. For Q10 I’ll include a region map + VPC config snippet. For Q29 I’ll attach the network diagram and the firewall rule export.

Rina (Security): I’ll take Q44 and Q76. For Q44 I’ll add KMS policy screenshots, a snippet of the DB encryption config, and a short policy blurb. For Q76 I’ll provide the current subprocessors CSV and a statement on onboarding controls.

Marc (Procurement - Opsidian): Quick note: legal prefers screenshots over raw config files for the initial pass. They still want the underlying configs if possible. Also, procurement needs the dates for the last pen test and SOC2.

Sam (Solutions Eng): Noted. I can generate annotated screenshots for the VPC and export JSON for the firewall rules. Will include annotations like "customer VPC peering" and masked IPs.

Rina (Security): Pen test date: 2024-09-12 (summary attached). SOC2: report 2024 redacted version is available. I'll upload both to the shared bucket.

upload-bot: Uploaded pen-test-summary-20240912.pdf, soc2-redacted-2024.pdf to gs://redwood-compliance/opsidian/ (permissions: view by link).

Taylor (Sales): Marc — do you need a formal attestation letter or is the bundle enough to start legal review?

Marc (Procurement - Opsidian): Bundle is fine to start. If legal needs an attestation later we’ll request it. Please include a one-paragraph plain-English answer for each SIG question; legal reviewers are non-technical.

Sam (Solutions Eng): Drafting plain-English answers now. Example for Q29: "Network isolation: Private deployment uses dedicated VPCs per customer with no cross-tenant routing. Peering is customer-initiated and requires IAM approval. See attached diagram." Good?

Rina (Security): That works. For Q44 plain-English: "Encryption: All persistent storage is encrypted at rest using customer-supplied or Redwood-managed keys via AWS KMS. Backup snapshots are encrypted, and key rotation occurs every 90 days. See attached KMS policy and snapshot config screenshot."

Sam (Solutions Eng): Uploaded network-diagram-annotated.png and vpc-firewall-export.json to gs://redwood-compliance/opsidian/. Added README mapping files to SIG Q numbers.

upload-bot: subprocessors-list.csv and kms-policy-screenshots.zip uploaded to gs://redwood-compliance/opsidian/.

Rina (Security): I redacted internal CSIRTs from the pen-test PDF and added a short summary. Also added q44_plain_answer.md and q76_plain_answer.md into the folder.

Taylor (Sales): I'm assembling the zip now: opsidian-sig-bundle-1768888888.zip. Target upload in 30 minutes.

Sam (Solutions Eng): Reminder: for Q10 include retention-policy-2024.md and region-map-2025.pdf (these are in the bucket).

Marc (Procurement - Opsidian): We received the view link. Thanks all. Legal will ping if they need deeper logs.

Rina (Security): Quick checklist before we close: Q10 (region map + retention doc) ✅, Q29 (network diagram + firewall export) ✅, Q44 (KMS screenshots + db-encryption-config) ✅, Q76 (subprocessors CSV + onboarding controls) ✅. I’ll sign off on the bundle once Taylor confirms the ZIP.

Taylor (Sales): ZIP uploaded to gs://redwood-compliance/opsidian/opsidian-sig-bundle-1768888888.zip. Shared view link to Marc.

upload-bot: opsidian-sig-bundle-1768888888.zip uploaded and link shared with users:marc@opsidian.com.

Marc (Procurement - Opsidian): Confirmed receipt. Legal review starts tomorrow morning. Appreciate the speed.

Taylor (Sales): Thanks team — will keep monitoring the thread for follow-ups. If legal requests attestation, Rina can draft an official letter.

Rina (Security): Happy to.

Sam (Solutions Eng): Closing out my to-dos. Ping me if any of the screenshots need tweaks.
